title: Strayhorn's death and Duke giving credit
summary: Strayhorn died in 1967 after sending Blood Count; Cootie agrees Duke always gave Billy credit.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: I know you did. I know you did. That's right. I want to talk about that. So let's -- I want to -- we're coming to that. So wait one second, now. Oh, yeah, Cootie, in '66, which was Dakar and Senegal, I think that must have been the Festival of the Arts, over there in Africa, because when he came back he wrote "La Plus Belle Africaine", which is a beautiful number.
That's a beautiful number. Now, '67, Strayhorn died. So Strayhorn had been sick about at least a year, then, hadn't he?
And that's when Strayhorn sent "Blood Count" over for the band at the record session, wasn't it?
Yeah. That must have been very hard for Duke, wasn't it? I mean, he really minded, didn't he?
Yeah. He did. He really minded.

Another thing that Duke did to show -- which exhibited what a big man he was, was the way he gratuitously and continuously gave people credit, didn't he? And I mean, all through the years he would always speak of Billy
He always, continuously spoke of Billy. And I mean, that's really not what you'd expect. Not what most people do, is it?
No. Not what most people do.
No. I mean, it wasn't even as if Billy was looking for it. Because he was like Duke in that way, too. He never pushed himself forward either, did he?
